beats.narration_slice: Two body outlines show different heat loss.
beats.visual: Two layered paper-cut human silhouettes stand in the same cool environment, one small and one giant, with soft amber heat cues drifting away from their surfaces.
beats.purpose: show that differently sized bodies lose heat differently
beats.visual_fingerprint: paired small and giant human cutout silhouettes side by side on a frosty blue ground with outward heat wisps, front comparison composition
beats.continuity: begin the scale comparison with a clear two-form setup

beats.narration_slice: Small and giant models lose warmth at different speeds.
beats.visual: The two paper-cut body models are shown at different moments of heat fading, with the smaller figure retaining a warmer glow while the giant figure has broader cooling areas.
beats.purpose: compare the speed of heat loss between sizes
beats.visual_fingerprint: small and giant anatomical paper models in a time-sequence-like frozen scene with different heat glow intensities, angled overhead view
beats.continuity: same scale experiment, shifted from comparison to heat behavior

beats.narration_slice: The giant model has more outside area and loses heat.
beats.visual: A giant paper-cut human form is surrounded by a larger exposed outer edge, with warm internal layers releasing heat into the surrounding cool air.
beats.purpose: show the larger outside area involved in heat loss
beats.visual_fingerprint: single giant layered body cutaway with expanded outer perimeter and heat escaping into blue atmosphere, low angle close composition
beats.continuity: moves from two-body comparison into the giant model's surface details

beats.narration_slice: The inner part of the body grows differently from outside area.
beats.visual: A giant paper-cut body is opened as a layered anatomical form, showing a deeper inner volume compared with its outer boundary layer.
beats.purpose: show that inner volume and outer area scale differently
beats.visual_fingerprint: large anatomical paper cross-section with nested ivory layers and surrounding blue space, top-down cutaway composition
beats.continuity: same giant model, revealing hidden internal structure

beats.narration_slice: The square-cube rule explains size changes outside area and volume.
beats.visual: A small paper cube-like body form expands into a much larger layered cube and body shape, showing surface layers and filled interior changing at different rates.
beats.purpose: explain the relationship between surface area and volume during scaling
beats.visual_fingerprint: abstract paper-cut scaling demonstration with nested cube forms and a human-shaped silhouette merging into the comparison, centered perspective
beats.continuity: transitions from anatomy to the underlying size principle

beats.narration_slice: Volume means the space inside a body.
beats.visual: A translucent layered paper-cut body shape reveals a filled inner region representing the space contained inside the form.
beats.purpose: show the meaning of volume as internal space
beats.visual_fingerprint: transparent layered anatomical shell with a glowing inner paper volume mass, centered close-up composition
beats.continuity: focuses on one concept from the previous scaling explanation

beats.narration_slice: An elephant-sized human may struggle with body heat.
beats.visual: An elephant-scale human paper-cut figure stands in a cool landscape while heat gathers around the body and cooling layers work harder.
beats.purpose: show the possible heat challenge of an elephant-sized human
beats.visual_fingerprint: towering human silhouette beside tiny environmental elements with amber heat stress cues, wide ground-level perspective
beats.continuity: returns the concept to a real imagined giant body scenario

beats.narration_slice: The models show bigger bodies change beyond height.
beats.visual: Several ascending paper-cut human forms show changing proportions, with the largest having altered limb and body relationships rather than simple enlargement.
beats.purpose: show that scaling changes body proportions
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-stage paper human scale progression arranged diagonally with visibly changing proportions, studio-like blue background
beats.continuity: uses the giant example to examine structural changes

beats.narration_slice: A giant human is not just a larger copy.
beats.visual: A giant paper-cut human stands beside a smaller version, with distinct layered anatomy and altered proportions emphasizing a different body design.
beats.purpose: show that giant bodies require different solutions than enlarged normal bodies
beats.visual_fingerprint: small human and transformed giant human facing each other in a full-bleed paper landscape, dramatic side composition
beats.continuity: concludes the scale lesson with the main takeaway

beats.visual: The giant human paper-cut figure is surrounded by adaptive cooling structures and environmental elements suggesting future ways to manage heat.

beats.visual_fingerprint: giant layered human in a calm blue thermal environment with new cooling forms around the body, wide final hero composition
